newsitem.title: UK: Copper finishes at highs on LME, aluminium firm.
newsitem.headline: Copper finishes at highs on LME, aluminium firm.

text.p: Base metal markets were more lively during Thursday afternoon's LME trading, as copper cleared important technical resistance en route to closing at the highs.
Aluminium was also firm, and closed conclusively above $1,600 after setting a new seven-month high, while there were gains also in most other markets.
Traders said overall LME sentiment is favouring the upside, and all markets were expected to benefit to varying degrees on the upside in the short term.
Even copper where long-term fundamentals are not promising, was being supported by current inventory tightness and has further upside potential, they said.
The market eventually cleared previously stubborn resistance around $2,250 during a more active afternoon session, running up to conclude the kerb at $2,270, a gain of $30 a tonne.
Traders expected a challenge of $2,280 resistance now heralding an attack on the more important level of $2,313 -- the recent high.
On stocks, expectations were that Friday's LME warehouse data would be little changed, and it was unlikely that there would be a big movement similar to Tuesday, they said.
Aluminium broke above $1,600 today, and eventually edged up to the top of the $1,600/1,610 resistance band, which put the market on course to swing up to $1,650.

There has been producer selling into the current rally, but traders were confident that Friday's LME stock data and IPAI producer inventory figures for November would be beneficial to sentiment. Prices closed at $1,610, up $20 from yesterday.

Aluminium alloy leapt higher today, with the gains only partly due to strong primary prices. Tightness of supplies has been reflected recently in the cash/threes contango narrowing to $15 from $25 three weeks ago.
Also, demand for the primary/alloy switch has been evident, with today's activity cutting this to $95 from $115 on Wednesday and compared with $170 at the start of the year.
Three months prices traded up to $1,530 a tonne, closing at $1,515, up $50 from yesterday.
Nickel prices shook off earlier uncertainty during the afternoon session, and resumed the strong uptrend seen so far this year by moving smartly higher.
Traders said buy-stops helped prices reach above $7,200 at one stage, although there was some resistance here ahead of the stronger hurdle pegged at $7,450.
Despite this last business was at $7,210, up $105 from yesterday, and well above the $7,040 low seen earlier.
Lead gained also during the afternoon session, largely helped by copper's renewed strength, although traders also cited current severe weather in Europe.
It was anticipated this would lead to increased replacement vehicle battery demand if it persisted. Last kerb trade was at $692, up $6.
Tin similarly climbed during the afternoon after a largely lacklustre morning spent at little changed levels. Final business was at $5,855, a $35 advance from yesterday.
However, zinc remained inhibited within a tight band, and prices finished the day at $1,063, down $2 after a session of little movement and light interest.
--Martin Hayes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8080
